title: Bradley goes firm-wide with Legora
summary: Bradley is rolling out Legora to more than 750 lawyers across 13 offices, as well as the business functions that support them.
body_markdown:
Legora, the agentic operating system for legal professionals, today announced that Bradley is adopting its platform enterprise-wide, to more than 750 lawyers across 13 offices in seven states and the District of Columbia.


The rollout supports every practice area of the firm, as well as knowledge management and business operations. For Bradley, the aim of the adoption is to expedite the path from instruction to first draft and reduce the number of internal delays that sit between a question and an answer.


“Legora gives our lawyers and business professionals an AI platform built specifically for legal work and allows us to spend more time using the judgment and strategic skills that drive better and more meaningful results for our clients,” said Jonathan M. Skeeters, Chairman of the Board and Managing Partner at Bradley. “This coordinated approach across the firm’s legal practices and business departments, along with this partnership with Legora, are consistent with Bradley’s culture of collaboration and one-firm mentality that drives success for our clients.”


Legora runs on Bradley’s own precedent and templates, within the controls a law firm requires: permissions and ethical walls that keep matter teams separated, citations that point back to the source so any output can be checked, and an audit trail of how each output is produced when using the platform. Judgment and accountability stay with the lawyer.


“With over 1,200 lawyers and business professionals across the firm, our knowledge management systems are a critical aspect of how we stay at the top of our profession,” said Rance Sapen, Chief Operating Officer at Bradley. “Legora is helping us streamline our work in a collaborative ecosystem, creating a working environment that improves work product and impacts outcomes.”


Across Bradley’s wide range of practice areas, Legora will support research, document review, and drafting on complex matters. Lawyers will use the platform to work through diligence, review large volumes of documents, and produce first drafts, while retaining full control over legal judgment and client strategy.


“Bradley put its whole firm on one system rather than handing a tool to a single practice group. That is what an agentic operating system is for. That strategy reflects a firm that’s ambitious and thinks about AI as infrastructure rather than a feature,” said Max Junestrand, CEO and Co-Founder of Legora.


About Bradley


For over 155 years, Bradley has combined skilled legal counsel with exceptional client service and unwavering integrity to assist a diverse range of corporate and individual clients in achieving their business goals. An Am Law 100 firm with 13 offices in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, North Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and the District of Columbia, Bradley's more than 750 lawyers represent regional, national and international clients in various industries, including banking and financial services, construction, energy, healthcare, life sciences, manufacturing, real estate, and technology, among many others.


About Legora


Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review, and drafting across complex matters. It is used by more than 130,000 legal professionals at more than 2,000 leading law firms and in-house legal teams across over 80 markets.
